standard_prerequisites: The situation fixing a map of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic space over B and the functors on Sch/B attached to a property of the base changed map
Commutation of pullbacks with base change, and commutation of the direct image along an affine morphism with base change
The adjunction between pullback and direct image for an affine morphism
Exactness and full faithfulness of the direct image functor along a closed immersion on quasi-coherent modules
core_obligations: After base change to T the identifications (i^*F)_T = i_T^*F_T and i_{T,*}H_T = (i_*H)_T hold, the first by commutativity of pullbacks and the second by the affine base change lemma, so u_T and v_T remain adjoint maps
Adjoint maps vanish together: u_T = 0 exactly when v_T = 0, which proves part one

For a closed immersion u_T factors as F_T -> i_{T,*}i_T^*F_T -> i_{T,*}H_T with the second arrow i_{T,*}v_T, and the unit of the adjunction together with the exact fully faithful embedding i_{T,*} shows u_T is surjective exactly when v_T is surjective
proof_roadmap: Base change the adjunction: verify both commutation identities and conclude u_T and v_T stay adjoint
Derive part one from vanishing of adjoint pairs
Derive part two from the unit factorization and exact full faithfulness of i_{T,*}
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the two functor equalities at source lines 1435-1446, label lemma-relate-zero-affine, whose proof occupies source lines 1448-1468. The proof is not a citation: it verifies the two base change commutation identities that keep u_T and v_T adjoint after pullback, derives the vanishing equivalence for adjoint pairs, and for the closed immersion case writes the unit factorization of u_T through i_{T,*} and uses exactness and full faithfulness of the direct image to transfer surjectivity. The counted statement records none of this.
